relevance_note: The paper describes 13 individually identifiable patients with succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase (SSADH) deficiency and their ALDH5A1 variants: 'The 13 patients with SSADH deficiency were from 12 non-consanguineous Chinese families'.
method_note: Read the Markdown full text, Table 1, Table 2 and the two table legends directly; no script transcribed a table. All 13 patients (the paper's own labels Patient 1 to Patient 13) are in scope and are the only people described individually; no relative rows were created because the only statement about relatives is a group one ('Next-generation sequencing was conducted in five patients (patients 2, 7, and 11-13) and their parents') and it gives no individual-level fact about any parent. cohort_size_as_stated = n_patients_reported = 13. The paper never uses 'proband' or 'index case' and never says its patients were published earlier, so is_proband and cites_prior_report_of_same_patients are false with span null. Table 2's 'Reported' column gives the reference for each variant ('[4]', 'This study', '[2, 8]'), not a per-patient source, and one patient's two variants can have different values, so source_reference_in_review is 'not reported' for every individual. Zygosity is 'not reported' everywhere: the paper never prints 'heterozygous' or 'compound heterozygous' and rule 8 forbids inferring zygosity from the Paternal/Maternal allele column. Inheritance is read from that per-patient 'Allele' column of Table 2 (the paper's own assignment of each allele to a parent), and the same cell is quoted in parental_testing_statement. variant_type is given only where the text names the class of that exact variant ('eight missense variants (c.454G > C, ...)', 'one frameshift variant (c.427del)', 'one nonsense variant (c.762C > G)', 'one insertion (c.206_222dup)', 'one deletion (c.85_116del)'); the authors' words 'insertion' and 'deletion' have no matching enum value so those two are 'other', and the six previously reported variants have no stated class. No functional assays were performed ('Our study did not include enzyme-activity analyses of the patients'), so functional_evidence_statement is 'not reported' everywhere; the Discussion sentences that speculate that certain missense variants 'dramatically reduced SSADH enzyme activity' are not assay results. Transcript NM_001080.3 and build hg19 are printed only in the Table 2 footnote; no g. coordinates are printed, so genomic_coordinates_as_stated is null. For phenotypic features I used Table 1's per-patient clinical-features cell plus text sentences that name the patient; counts without names ('Seven patients (53.8%) had epileptic seizures', 'Sleep disturbances were observed in 10 (76.9%) patients', 'Dystonia was found in seven patients (53.8%)', 'Eight patients (61.5%) experienced language developmental delays') were never assigned to individuals, so speech or language impairment, ataxia, dyskinesia, ADHD, anxiety, obsessive-compulsive traits and aggression are 'not reported' for everyone (the Discussion sentence 'The children exhibited varied forms of intellectual and motor retardation, and showed major motor and fine motor skills and language development severely behind their peers [12]' was not used either, as it is a literature-attributed generalisation). Group statements that name the group were used with evidence_basis 'inferred from group statement': 'All 13 patients ... experienced psychomotor retardation, including delayed head-raising, sitting, and standing up in comparison with their normal peers' (intellectual disability, gross or fine motor deficits) and the normal investigations of all 13 patients, for which I recorded the abnormality each rules out per the normal-findings rule ('abnormal liver and kidney function', 'abnormal serum electrolyte levels', 'abnormal blood amino acid and acylcarnitine profile', all excluded). No legend defines '-' or a similar symbol as absent, so no table cell was read as excluded. Contradictions and oddities: the EEG paragraph is internally inconsistent ('Electroencephalography was performed in six patients. One (Patient 4) showed increased background slow activity; one (Patient 2) showed suspected epileptic seizure; and six patients showed generalized spikes, spike-and-waves, and slow waves'), so only Patients 4 and 2 have EEG findings; Patient 13's schizophrenia is contradictory ('misdiagnosed as “schizophrenia” aged 14y' in Table 1 versus 'Patient 13 was diagnosed as showing schizophrenia at the age of 14 years' in the text), so both an observed and an excluded phenotypic row are given and the checklist item stays 'not reported'; Patient 10's maternal c.1344-2del is cited '[7]' while the same variant in Patient 12 is '[6]'; the text writes c.617delT and c.427delA while Table 2 writes c.617del and c.427del; dystonia is counted in seven patients but only Patient 8's Table 1 row lists dystonia; Table 1 gives Patient 9 a peak urine 4-hydroxybutyrate acid of 1.7 mmol/mol Cr while the text calls all values elevated. Table 2 puts a patient's two variants on two rows and leaves the Patient cell empty on the second row; those continuation rows are the spans used for the maternal variants. Table 1 cells and the Table 2 and legend separators contain non-breaking spaces (U+00A0) and thin spaces (U+2009), written here as \u00a0 and \u2009 escapes so the spans match the file exactly. 'Emotional disturbance' for Patients 6 and 13 was mapped to the checklist item 'depression or mood fluctuation'. Two further judgement calls: the sentence 'Among these patients, Patient 13 was diagnosed as showing schizophrenia at the age of 14 years, indicating that hallucinations, delusions, and schizophrenic behaviors were more common in older children and adolescents' does not clearly assert hallucinations or delusions for Patient 13 herself, so 'psychotic symptoms (hallucinations or delusions)' was left 'not reported' for her; and the peak urine 4-hydroxybutyrate acid values in Table 1 are recorded under severity_or_detail rather than as a separate feature, since the schema has no field for the value.
